storm.summary_layperson: No thunderstorm risk expected at the cove this evening — clear skies, dry air, and a fading northwest breeze, with nothing on radar anywhere near the area.
storm.local_effect_blurb: The Sound's cooling gap is only 5.2°F right now and closes to nothing by about 4:13 PM as the afternoon air cools — the marine layer is essentially gone before this window even starts, but it doesn't matter tonight since there's no storm for it to weaken anyway.
storm.detail_html:
The regional picture is clean: no active NWS alerts, no radar echo anywhere near Riverside on the KOKX scan, and instability is essentially zero (CAPE 0 J/kg). The Area Forecast Discussion mentions only a generic "slight chance of a thunderstorm" with no specifics on timing or location, and the NWS point forecast simply calls for sunny skies with a light northwest wind. There is no storm cell to track and no arrival estimate to compute this cycle.

The cove's usual defense — the cool Long Island Sound acting as a marine layer that chokes storms crossing it — is a non-factor tonight for two reasons. First, there's nothing approaching to choke. Second, even if there were, the air–water gap is only 5.2°F at 4 PM and is projected to close to essentially zero by around 4:13 PM as the afternoon air cools toward evening, meaning the protective buffer runs out right at the start of the 5–10 PM window regardless.

Most likely outcome for the cove and every surrounding town alike: a dry, clear, quiet evening with nothing to differentiate one location from another, since there's no storm activity in play to be mitigated or amplified by local geography.

What would change this call: any new convective development tracking in from the west or northwest overnight, or an upgrade in the AFD's confidence in thunderstorm potential. Neither is currently indicated by the HRRR guidance or the latest AFD.

wind.tactics_blurb: This is a wait-it-out evening, not a bank-one-side evening — fading gradient wind with no sea breeze to lean on, and current readings running stronger and more easterly than the model expects. Stay centered, stay flexible for lulls and shifts, and don't commit hard to either side.
wind.tactics_detail_html:
This is a gradient-wind day, not a sea-breeze day. Only 5% of coastal stations show the southerly flow that would signal a thermal sea breeze building, and the air–water temperature difference ("deltaT," the gap that drives the thermal) is 5.2°F — below the roughly 8°F gate the cove needs to build a mature sea breeze. So the sea-breeze direction-maturation correction does not apply tonight; the raw model wind is used as-is.

HRRR shows the leftover northwest gradient flow fading fast through the window: about 7 kt at 5 PM, down to 4 kt by 6 PM and 3 kt by 7 PM, backing slightly from NNW toward N as it goes. With sunset at 6:58 PM and no thermal engine to replace the dying gradient, expect the evening to keep settling into light and variable conditions.

Worth flagging: HRRR is forecasting NNW wind, but the live readings at Riverside YC (9.6 kt 10-minute average, gusting to 15.7 kt, from NNE) and the offshore buoy (11.9 kt gusting 17.5 kt, also NNE) are both running noticeably stronger and more easterly than the model right now — an 84° direction divergence. That's not enough to trigger a correction on a non-thermal day, but it's a reason to treat the “goes very light” forecast with some caution, especially in the 5–6 PM hours.

With no dominant thermal and a weakening, directionally uncertain gradient, there's no reliable geographic favorite on the course tonight — stay center rather than banking on one side.

What racers will feel: 2–7 kt is light-air sailing for the whole fleet. Prioritize boat-handling smoothness and mode over sailing a fixed angle, expect frequent lulls, and don't be surprised if the fleet splits on pressure rather than on a structural side advantage.

Model coverage runs out after 7 PM this cycle, so the 8–10 PM rows are an estimate based on the observed decay trend, not direct HRRR output — treat those hours with extra caution.
